title: Pre-flip docs: keychain prompt wording, public README, idempotent supersede step
description: Pre-flip docs and runbook follow-ups from the Opus reviews of opum-ai/ward-cli#232 and #235 (both merged). README.md goes public with the repository tonight. (1) README and install runbook step 7: any other build (an upgrade, or a checkout build you are replacing) is expected to prompt; the interactive dialog is not yet measured. (2) README: drop "Once/Until the repository is public". (3) Install runbook rollback: there is no migration back, reinstall the newest release. (4) Publish runbook step 6: idempotent (append the superseded line only if grep -qxF finds it absent), gh release edit v0.1.0 gets --latest=false, and the flip gate text "step 6 is done" is pinned in a test. (5) verify-published-release.sh: pass -R to release view and download; the fake codesign asserts its path is the downloaded file.

acceptanceCriteria.text: README and install runbook step 7 say any other build is expected to prompt and the dialog is not yet measured
README no longer says Once or Until the repository is public
Publish runbook step 6 is idempotent, uses --latest=false, and a test pins step 6 and the flip gate text
verify-published-release.sh passes -R to gh release view and download, and the fake codesign asserts the downloaded path
bun run check, lore check and validate --strict pass

implementationNotes: Landed: opum-ai/ward-cli#242 (squash ae586d6, 2026-11-01), Opus APPROVE at 5fb1621, CI 41329481762 green. Mutation results, run before the PR with the script restored each time: removing -R from gh release view turns 14 of 16 verify-script cases red (the fake gh requires it); pointing the strict verify at the local file instead of the downloaded one turns 5 red (the fake codesign asserts the downloaded path); clean is 16 of 16. Public-text grep over README.md, SECURITY.md and the install runbook for Once/Until the repository, tracker and decision ids, opum-fleet and repository is private returned nothing. bun run check 1152 pass. LOWs filed as one follow-up task, not a re-head.
